title: Gene Therapy Gave Deaf Children Their Hearing Back.
summary: A one-time gene therapy infusion restored meaningful hearing in 9 of 12 children with profound inherited deafness, no implants required. One three-year-old went from near-total deafness to hearing in the normal range within weeks.

title: America Passed 80,000 Public Fast-Charging Ports
summary: America passed 80,000 public fast-charging ports after 4,106 were added in a single quarter, 73% of new ports at 250 kW or more, with a record 17.6 million charging sessions in July.

title: 3,000 Shelf-Scanning Robots Now Roam Stores Worldwide
summary: Simbe completed a 3,000-unit global rollout of Tally shelf-scanning robots, including Kroger's 500th, with retailers reporting steep drops in out-of-stocks and pricing errors.

title: Tanzania Brought School to 751 Children With Disabilities
summary: Tanzania's new inclusive education strategy brought schooling to 751 children with disabilities through home- and hospital-based learning, 440 laptops and tablets, over 522,000 Braille and large-print books, and compulsory sign-language training for student teachers.

title: Record Quarter for US Clean Power as 17.1 GW Came Online
summary: 164 utility-scale clean energy projects came online in the US in a single quarter, up 45% on the year, pushing total clean capacity to about 388 gigawatts. The quarter included SunZia, the largest land-based wind project in American history.

title: An Autonomous AI Triaged Skin Cancer Referrals Across Two UK Hospitals
summary: A CE-marked AI autonomously discharged 25 to 31% of urgent suspected skin cancer referrals across two UK hospitals, 8,391 patients, saving 2,851 clinician hours. The first large-scale real-world autonomous AI deployment in a cancer pathway.

title: GM Started Shipping EVs With Fully Recycled Battery Cells
summary: GM's closed-loop pilot turned 80 end-of-life battery packs into cathode material with 100% recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese, certified to match virgin material, and the first EVs carrying those cells are now shipping to customers.

title: Two Humanoid Robots Joined a Live Packaging Line in Korea
summary: CJ Logistics put two dual-arm humanoids to work stuffing cushioning into boxes at a fulfillment center, the first live logistics humanoid deployment in South Korea.

title: AI Eye Screening in Primary Care Halved the Cost of Catching Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: Autonomous AI eye screening in a Canadian primary-care clinic completed 93.6% of exams on the spot and cut the cost per diagnosed case of diabetic retinopathy roughly in half.

title: A Smartphone App Guided Blind Users 13% Faster With 41% Fewer Bumps
summary: Harvard's Mobilio smartphone app, with pedestrian-view AI and personalized audio cues, guided 14 blind and low-vision participants 13% faster with 41% fewer bumps, at reliability comparable to a human guide.

title: A Double Neural Bypass Rewired a Paralyzed Man's Nervous System.
summary: Keith Thomas, completely paralyzed since 2020, regained hand movement and wrist sensation through brain implants paired with AI-decoded stimulation. Remarkably, the gains persisted more than two years after stimulation stopped.

title: A Prosthetic Hand That Learns Each Amputee's Unique Muscle Signals
summary: A 3D-scanned, 3D-printed sleeve with magnetic sensors plus individualized AI decoded 19 hand gestures in real time for ten participants, including three amputees. It stayed accurate after 7,500 force cycles.

title: A 5.5-Pound Hip Exoskeleton Cut Stroke Survivors' Walking Effort by 18%
summary: A portable hip exoskeleton offloaded about 30% of hip work for stroke survivors with hemiparesis, cutting walking effort 18%. Some gait gains persisted after the device came off.

title: Trimming a Rice Gene Lifted Yields 25% and Drought Tolerance
summary: Chicago scientists trimmed a section of rice's own ALKBH9 and ALKBH10 genes, no foreign DNA, and boosted harvests 20 to 25% with better drought and heat tolerance. Published in Nature Genetics.

title: The World Installed a Record 664 GW of Solar in 2025.
summary: The world installed a record 664 gigawatts of solar in 2025, pushing the global fleet past 3 terawatts, triple its size four years ago. Solar now supplies about 9% of all electricity generated on Earth.

title: A Resistance Robot Taught Kids With SMA to Stand Up on Their Own
summary: A 2.1-pound knee robot that resists rather than assists movement helped six children with spinal muscular atrophy gain 130% quadriceps strength. All of them can now rise from a chair unassisted.

title: A Humanoid Robot Helped Build 30,000 BMWs Over an 11-Month Run
summary: A Figure 02 humanoid worked 10-hour shifts at BMW's Spartanburg plant inserting sheet-metal parts for welding at better than 99% accuracy per shift, helping build 30,000 cars over an 11-month run.

title: AI Thermal Imaging and Drones Now Guard Kenya's Wildlife Parks
summary: The Kenya Wildlife Service embedded AI thermal imaging, drones, and EarthRanger into daily ranger operations, with real-time poacher alerts across its parks.

title: The World Installed a Record 112 GW of Grid Batteries in 2025.
summary: Grid battery installations jumped 48% to a record 112 gigawatts in 2025, ten times the 2021 level, as lithium-ion prices kept falling. Storage is finally catching up with the solar boom.

title: One in Four Cars Sold Worldwide Was Electric in 2025.
summary: More than 20 million electric cars sold in 2025, a full quarter of all cars sold worldwide and a first-ever milestone. Emerging markets doubled their sales in a single year.

title: AI Scribes Gave Doctors 16 Minutes Back Per Patient Visit
summary: A JAMA multisite study across five academic centers found ambient AI scribes cut clinician documentation by 16 minutes per patient visit in real clinics, a modest but genuine productivity gain.

title: Green Hydrogen Unlocked Low-Grade Ore for Climate-Neutral Steel
summary: A Namibian pilot converted 80 tonnes of low-grade iron ore into direct-reduced iron using green hydrogen, unlocking ore grades conventional green-steel routes cannot touch.

title: An Open AI Model for Protein Structures Released Its Full Training Stack
summary: OpenFold3 released its training datasets, weights, and code under permissive licenses: an open protein-structure AI competitive with AlphaFold3.

title: A Baby Got the World's First Personalized CRISPR Therapy. A Year Later, He's Walking and Talking.
summary: KJ Muldoon was born with a fatal metabolic disorder and no treatment options. Six months later a bespoke CRISPR edit built for his exact mutation had him walking, talking, and eating protein safely, and his case pushed the FDA to create a faster path for personalized therapies.

title: Closed-Loop Insulin Pumps Beat Sensor Pumps Across 27 Trials
summary: A meta-analysis of 27 randomized trials with over 1,000 participants found hybrid closed-loop insulin pumps raised time in range 8.8 points over sensor-augmented pumps, supporting NHS England's expansion plan.

title: Orange County's Water Recycler Passed Half a Trillion Gallons
summary: Orange County's Groundwater Replenishment System, the world's largest advanced purification plant for potable reuse, passed half a trillion gallons over 18 years, now recycling 100% of reclaimable flows for up to 2.5 million people.

title: A Copper Smelter Now Heats Thousands of Hamburg Homes
summary: Waste heat from the Aurubis copper smelter now travels 3.7 km into Hamburg's district heating network, warming thousands of homes and saving up to 120,000 tonnes of CO2 a year.

title: China Approved the World's First Commercial Brain Implant for Paralysis.
summary: China approved the first brain implant for commercial use in paralysis, with Neuracle's NEO restoring hand movement. A paralyzed hand moving again is not a gadget; it is independence, returned.

title: A Malaria Vaccine Reached a Refugee Camp. Child Deaths Fell by Half.
summary: MSF completed the first full malaria vaccine campaign ever run in a refugee camp, fully vaccinating 2,100 young children in Ethiopia's Kule camp. In the months after, the camp hospital recorded roughly half as many child malaria deaths as the year before.

title: A Brain Implant Let a Paralyzed Man Drive a Wheelchair and Command a Robot Dog
summary: A man paralyzed since 2022 steers a smart wheelchair outdoors, sends a robot dog on errands, and does paid remote computer work, all through a fully implanted wireless brain-computer interface with under 100ms latency.

title: An AI Bionic Hand That Grasps Without Making Amputees Think
summary: Proximity and pressure sensing plus a neural net let a commercial bionic hand auto-position its fingers, so four amputees got a more secure grip with far less mental effort.

title: India Hit 50% Non-Fossil Power Capacity Five Years Early
summary: India crossed 50% non-fossil power capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of its Paris target, after adding a record 48 to 50 gigawatts of renewables in a single year.

title: Hospital-Level Care Came Home to Rural America
summary: A 161-patient randomized trial of hospital-level care at home: wireless chest-sticker telemetry, fanny-pack IV pumps, handheld lab meters. Costs 27% lower with early transfer, patients walked 700 more steps a day, satisfaction 88 versus 46.

title: 2Africa, the Longest Subsea Cable Ever Built, Is Complete
summary: 2Africa, the longest subsea cable ever built at 45,000 km around the continent, is complete. The hard part now is the middle and last mile getting that capacity to people.

title: Perovskite Solar Cells Hit a Record 27.2% Efficiency.
summary: Researchers set a new 27.2% efficiency record for perovskite solar cells with a simple potassium additive that also made the cells far more durable. Cheap, high-efficiency panels just got meaningfully closer.

title: Solar-Powered Links Brought 10,000 Rural Kenyans Online for School
summary: Kenya's education network wired 20 rural institutions through university hubs with solar backup, bringing 10,000 rural Kenyans online for school. One college's 100 idle donated computers became a working lab.

title: Gene Therapy Cured 95% of Children Born Without an Immune System.
summary: In the largest and longest-tracked cohort of its kind, 59 of 62 children born with ADA-SCID were cured by lentiviral gene therapy, with 100% survival over seven and a half years. Kids who once would not have lived past two are now in school and playing sports.

title: A Rice-Grain Chip Let Blind Patients Read Again.
summary: A rice-grain-sized retinal implant paired with AR glasses restored reading vision in 84% of patients with untreatable macular degeneration. On average they gained five lines on the vision chart.

title: The World's First Pressure-Geothermal Storage Plant Built in Texas
summary: Sage Geosystems built the world's first pressure-geothermal storage plant in Texas in 12 months: engineered underground fractures store energy at 70 to 75% round-trip efficiency with up to 17 hours of discharge. It connected to the grid in December 2025.

title: Switzerland Released Apertus, a Fully Open Multilingual AI Model
summary: EPFL, ETH Zurich and CSCS released Apertus, a multilingual AI model trained on public infrastructure with weights, data, and training recipes all public under Apache 2.0. AI for the public good, not a commercial launch.

title: Sensors on Power Lines Unlocked Nearly 50% More Grid Capacity in Minnesota
summary: Great River Energy's dynamic line rating deployment, the largest in the US by sensor count, found 48.92% more capacity on a pilot transmission line, going from pilot to full deployment in under nine months.

title: A Bionic Knee That Feels Like Part of Your Body.
summary: MIT built a prosthetic knee anchored to bone and wired into the nervous system, and the first two amputees to receive it walked faster, climbed stairs, and said it felt like part of themselves. Published in Science.

title: Lab-Grown Islet Cells Freed 10 of 12 Diabetics From Insulin.
summary: A single infusion of lab-grown islet cells left 10 of 12 adults with severe type 1 diabetes fully insulin-independent a year later. All twelve were free of dangerous low-blood-sugar episodes, a scalable alternative to donor transplants.

title: A Beach-Cleaning Robot Joined the Great Lakes Cleanup.
summary: Canada's first BeBot, a remote-controlled beach-cleaning robot, started work on Ontario's Great Lakes shores in summer 2025. It sieves microplastics from sand at up to 3,000 square meters per hour.

title: The World's Largest Reverse-Osmosis Desalination Plant Certified
summary: Saudi Arabia's Al Khobar RO2 was certified the world's largest reverse-osmosis desalination plant at 670,852 cubic meters a day. Its sister plant set the world record for the lowest RO energy use.

title: AI Tutoring Lifted Nigerian Students' English Scores.
summary: A World Bank trial gave Nigerian students GPT-4-powered after-school tutoring and watched English scores rise by 0.31 standard deviations, with the biggest gains for girls. At $48 per student, it ranks among the most cost-effective education interventions ever measured.

title: A Plant That Turns Captured CO2 Into Limestone Opened in Norfolk
summary: Mission Zero's electrochemical plant in Norfolk pulls 250 tonnes of CO2 a year from the air and turns it into carbon-negative limestone for bricks and concrete: the world's first fully integrated direct-air-capture-to-building-materials plant, operating commercially.

title: Cyborg Cockroaches Joined a Real Earthquake Rescue.
summary: After the March 2025 Myanmar earthquake, Singapore's rescue team deployed ten camera-equipped cyborg cockroaches into rubble too tight for humans or dogs. A world first for the technology, in a real disaster.

title: A Sunlight-and-Seawater Device Makes Green Hydrogen and Drinking Water
summary: A low-cost device that needs only sunlight and seawater to produce green hydrogen and clean drinking water, with no grid power required.

title: A Brain Implant Steered a Robotic Arm for Seven Months Without Recalibration
summary: UCSF researchers showed a paralyzed man could control a robotic arm for reaching and grasping for a record seven months, because the AI adapted to small day-to-day shifts in brain activity. Previous implants typically needed recalibration within days.

title: A Prosthetic Liner You Adjust From Your Phone
summary: A silicone prosthetic liner with pressurized channels lets amputees adjust the fit in real time from a smartphone. Six trial users reported far fewer frustrating fits, meaning fewer blisters, sores, and returns to the wheelchair.

title: A Bone-Anchored Implant Got an Amputee Walking Again After a Decade
summary: After a decade of failed socket prostheses, a titanium implant anchored directly into the patient's femur got him walking unaided. He even senses the ground through the bone itself.

title: A Prosthetic Hand That Restores Touch and Cut Phantom Pain by 90%
summary: Spinal and peripheral nerve stimulation let an amputee distinguish object sizes by touch through a prosthesis, with no training. Phantom limb pain fell 90%.

title: A Rescue Robot Pulled Tourists From Rough Water in Hainan
summary: A U-shaped water rescue robot pulled struggling tourists from the surf in Hainan during its first Spring Festival deployment. It is now in service in Fujian and Guangdong too.

title: A Brain Implant Decoded Finger Movements to Fly a Drone
summary: A quadriplegic patient steered a virtual drone through obstacle courses using only decoded finger movements from his motor cortex. Three independent finger groups, read straight from the brain (Nature Medicine).

title: A Dual-Arm Robot Picks Apples at Near-Human Speed
summary: A dual-arm harvester built with Michigan State picks an apple every three seconds using AI vision, at near-human speed. The USDA positions it as a commercially viable answer to orchard labor costs.

title: Stem Cells Reversed Type 1 Diabetes in a Woman.
summary: A reprogrammed stem cell transplant reversed Type 1 diabetes in a woman, reported in Nature. A milestone for a disease once thought irreversible.

title: Blue Origin Made Solar Cells From Moon Dust.
summary: Blue Origin figured out how to make solar cells from Moon dust. With Blue Alchemist, the lunar surface could power its own future.

title: Gene Editing Might Cure HIV. The First Trial Results Are In.
summary: A startup's CRISPR approach to curing HIV has reported its first trial results. An old dream of medicine is being tested in the real world.

title: AI and Automation Are Collapsing the Drug Discovery Timeline.
summary: AI and automation are shrinking the drug discovery timeline, finding the right drug for the right patient faster. Speed that saves lives.

title: CRISPR's Next Act: Fighting Climate Change and Feeding the World.
summary: The CRISPR pioneers are aiming gene editing at climate change and world hunger. After medicine, the next act is the planet itself.

title: Exoskeleton Technology Could Redefine Disability.
summary: Exoskeleton technology is poised to redefine disability, making wheelchairs optional rather than inevitable. Standing, walking, and meeting the world at eye level again: that is what progress feels like.

title: Paralyzed With a Severed Spinal Cord, He Walks Again.
summary: With a severed spinal cord, he walked again after an implant bridged his injury. Medicine just did the miraculous.

title: A New Drug Delays Type 1 Diabetes in Kids.
summary: A new drug can delay type 1 diabetes in kids, buying them a full, normal childhood. Sometimes the best gift is more time.

title: The Hubble Is Falling. SpaceX Might Give It a Lift.
summary: The Hubble is falling, and SpaceX plus a billionaire backer are exploring a mission to lift it back up. Even our greatest telescopes deserve a second act.

title: The Living Lights That Could Cut Our Energy Use.
summary: Scientists are exploring bioluminescence, nature's own glow, as a way to light cities and cut energy use. Streets lit by living light: quieter, softer, and gentler on the planet.

title: Can Nuclear Fusion Put the Brakes on Climate Change?
summary: The New Yorker examined whether nuclear fusion could help slow climate change, laying out the science and the stakes. The dream of clean, near-limitless energy is still alive, and still worth chasing.

title: The Material That "Learns" Like a Sea Slug.
summary: Nickel oxide, a humble material, showed learning behaviors like a sea slug's: habituation and sensitization in its electrical responses. Matter that learns could one day become AI hardware that sips power instead of gulping it.

title: He Typed 90 Characters a Minute Using Only His Thoughts.
summary: A paralyzed man typed 90 characters a minute just by imagining handwriting, decoded by a Stanford brain implant. His thoughts became words at smartphone speed: communication, restored.

title: Alphabet's Wing Drones Hit 100,000 Deliveries.
summary: Alphabet's Wing drones crossed 100,000 deliveries, proof that the quiet work of delivery drones is paying off. Slowly, then suddenly.

title: Overnight Success Takes Decades: The mRNA Story.
summary: The mRNA miracle was decades in the making, built on years of patient, unglamorous work. Overnight success takes decades.

title: The Battery Made of Rust That Stores Power for 100 Hours.
summary: Form Energy's iron-air battery stores power for 100 hours at a tenth of lithium's cost, using rust. The humble battery just got heroic.

title: A Brain Implant Turned a Paralyzed Man's Thoughts Into Words.
summary: A brain implant turned a paralyzed man's thoughts directly into words, giving him back his voice. Communication, restored from within.

title: An mRNA Vaccine Fully Immunized Mice Against Malaria.
summary: An mRNA vaccine fully protected mice against malaria in trials. The same platform that fought COVID is now taking aim at one of humanity's oldest killers.

title: The Malaria Vaccine That Beat Expectations at 77% Efficacy.
summary: A malaria vaccine beat expectations with 77% efficacy, the first to clear the WHO's 75% bar, and it costs about $2 a dose. A landmark win against a global killer.

title: The FDA Approved VR Movies as a Treatment for Lazy Eye.
summary: The FDA approved VR movies as real therapy for kids' lazy eye. Amblyopia treatment just became movie night.

title: Your Cough Has a Sound. AI Can Hear Disease in It.
summary: AI can hear disease in a cough, turning a smartphone into a respiratory diagnostic tool. A simple sound check could catch illness early.

title: Drones Flew Blood to a Remote Hospital in 18 Minutes.
summary: In Uttarakhand, drones delivered blood to a remote hospital in just 18 minutes, skipping terrain that once meant hours of travel. A beautiful leapfrog moment, where the sky becomes the fastest road to care.

title: The CAD Program for Designing Organisms From Scratch.
summary: GP-write's genome CAD program lets scientists design organisms the way engineers design circuits, on a screen, before they are built. Biology is getting the drafting tools that made software and chips scale.

title: An AI App Is Reading Chest X-Rays for TB in Rural India.
summary: Qure.ai's AI reads chest X-rays for tuberculosis in rural India, bringing expert diagnosis where doctors are scarce. Healthcare capacity, multiplied by software.

title: The World's Best Hope for Enough Covid Vaccine.
summary: The Serum Institute's massive manufacturing scale-up became the world's best hope for enough vaccine. Scale, it turns out, is a superpower.

title: Europe Approved the First Artificial Heart for Sale.
summary: Europe approved Carmat's artificial heart for sale, a device born from aerospace engineering. A heart built like a spacecraft, now pumping blood in real chests: medicine borrowing from the stars.

title: A Robotic Teddy Bear Is Making Hospitalized Kids Feel Better.
summary: MIT's Huggable, a robotic teddy bear, helped more than 50 hospitalized kids feel better in a Pediatrics study. Sometimes the best medicine is a warm, patient friend.

title: Gene Therapies for Rare Diseases Are Here.
summary: One-shot gene therapies for rare diseases have arrived, turning lifelong conditions into solvable problems. Now the fight moves to making them affordable.

title: A Bold Effort to Cure HIV Using CRISPR.
summary: Scientists are making a bold attempt to cure HIV with CRISPR, cutting the virus out at its genetic root. Audacious science for a historic goal.

title: Old Phones and Smart Software Are Catching Illegal Loggers.
summary: Discarded phones, tucked into the rainforest, listen for the buzz of chainsaws and sound the alarm. Old tech is becoming the forest's best defender.

title: Verily's AI Is Diagnosing Diabetic Blindness in Rural India.
summary: Verily's AI is up and running in South India, diagnosing diabetic blindness where eye specialists are scarce. Sight saved by software, delivered to places the healthcare system barely reaches.

title: UPS Got the FAA Nod for Widespread Drone Deliveries.
summary: UPS won FAA approval for widespread drone deliveries, with health packages first in line. Medicine by air is moving from experiment to infrastructure, and the sky is becoming a supply route.

title: The Visor That Diagnoses a Stroke in Half a Minute.
summary: A simple visor can diagnose a stroke in 30 seconds with 92% accuracy, far above the 40 to 89% of standard emergency exams. Faster answers mean faster treatment, and brain cells saved by the minute.

title: SpaceX Took the Commercial Launch Crown From Russia.
summary: SpaceX overtook Russia as the world's most prolific commercial launcher, reshaping who gets to space. Competition lifted the whole industry.

title: A Teenager Built an AI That Diagnoses Her Grandfather's Eye Disease.
summary: Kavya Kopparapu built an AI that diagnoses her grandfather's eye disease using a smartphone and a 3D-printed lens. A teenager, a phone, and care in action.

title: AI Can Hear a Heart Attack in Your 911 Call.
summary: An AI system can hear cardiac arrest in a 911 caller's voice, sometimes better than human dispatchers. Every second counts, and now the phone can help.

title: The Armada of Saildrones Mapping the Oceans.
summary: A fleet of autonomous saildrones is mapping our oceans and gathering research data on its own. The wind is doing the driving while science rides along.

title: How Robots Are Making Better Drugs, Faster.
summary: Robots are now helping make better drugs, faster. Automation in the lab is accelerating the path from molecule to medicine.

title: Robots to Make Robots at ABB's $150M Factory.
summary: At ABB's $150 million factory, robots build robots. Automation is now manufacturing itself, and the future is assembling fast.

title: The FDA Approved the First Blood Sugar Monitor Without Finger Pricks.
summary: The FDA approved the first blood sugar monitor that needs no finger pricks, sparing diabetics thousands of tiny stabs. Small mercies are still mercies, and this one touches millions of fingertips.

title: Nanorobots That Swim Through Your Body to Deliver Medicine Are Coming.
summary: Tiny robots that swim through your body, deliver medicine exactly where it is needed, then dissolve away. The future of treatment may be smaller than a speck of dust.

title: Gene Therapy Made Deaf Mice Hear Again.
summary: Gene therapy ferried healthy genes into the inner ears of deaf mice, and they could hear again. A virus doing good, for once.

title: ISRO Launched 104 Satellites on One Rocket.
summary: ISRO launched 104 satellites on a single rocket, a world record set aboard the famously frugal PSLV. India's space program keeps proving that ingenuity beats big budgets.

title: The Robot With Its Head in the Cloud.
summary: This warehouse robot doesn't just pick boxes, it shares what it learns with a hive mind of its peers. Every robot gets smarter from every shift.

title: The App That Diagnoses Genetic Disorders at a Glance.
summary: An app can diagnose genetic disorders at a glance, doing in minutes what took doctors 16 years. Facial recognition is becoming a lifeline for rare diseases.

title: Asked Via a Mind-Reading Device, Locked-In Patients Said "I Love to Live."
summary: Asked through a brain-computer interface, three of four fully locked-in ALS patients said they love to live. A quiet, profound answer: technology giving a voice to those the world assumed had gone silent.

title: An AI Recreated a Nobel-Winning Physics Experiment in One Hour.
summary: An Australian National University AI recreated a Nobel-winning physics experiment in a single hour, learning the Bose-Einstein condensate setup from scratch. Machines that learn like scientists.

title: The $1,000 Braille Tablet Made of Microfluidic Bubbles.
summary: A braille tablet built on microfluidic bubbles promises full-page tactile graphics for under $1,000, a fraction of today's costs. Charts, graphs, and whole pages, finally touchable for blind readers.

title: ISRO Launched 20 Satellites on a Single Rocket.
summary: ISRO packed 20 satellites onto a single rocket and put them all in orbit in about 26 minutes. Efficiency at rocket scale.

title: A Soft Exosuit Is Helping Stroke Victims Walk Again.
summary: A low-cost, low-tech soft exosuit from Harvard is helping stroke victims walk again. Gentle robotics, enormous human impact.

title: The Painting Robot That Didn't Steal Anyone's Job.
summary: This painting robot did not replace its human coworkers, it transformed what they could do together. A story about robots that lift people up.

title: A Brain Chip Gave a Paralyzed Man His Hand Back.
summary: A brain chip gave a paralyzed man control of his own hand again. Thought became movement, and independence came back with it.

title: "For Us, This Technology Is a Game-Changer": Europe's Emergency Workers Turn to Drones.
summary: Europe's emergency workers are turning to drones as game-changers for rescues and disasters. Eyes in the sky, help on the way.

title: Sesame Phone: A Hands-Free Smartphone for Paralyzed Users.
summary: Sesame Phone gives paralyzed users a fully hands-free smartphone, controlled by head movements. Independence, one glance at a time.

title: Ford's Driverless Cars Passed the Snow Test.
summary: Ford's driverless cars passed the snow test, navigating one of driving's hardest conditions. Winter just met its match.

title: The Robot Surgeon That Stitches Better Than Humans.
summary: Johns Hopkins' STAR robot stitches with submillimeter precision, and it outstitched its own inventors. The robot surgeon is setting a new bar for delicate surgery.

title: CRISPR Offers Hope for Muscular Dystrophy.
summary: Gene editing is offering new hope to people with muscular dystrophy. CRISPR research is moving toward treatments for a disease that once had none.

title: The Ingenious Way Iranians Beam Banned Data Over Satellite TV.
summary: Iranians found an ingenious way to beam banned data in over satellite TV. When the internet is blocked, creativity finds a signal.

title: Stem Cell Surgery Regrew Eye Lenses in 12 Children.
summary: Stem cell surgery regrew functional eye lenses in 12 children born with cataracts. Young patients healed themselves, with a little help from science.

title: The Drone That Maps, Finds, and Detonates Landmines.
summary: This drone maps, finds, and detonates landmines 20 times faster and 200 times cheaper. A landmine-free world within a decade is suddenly thinkable.

title: World Energy Hit a Turning Point: Solar Cheaper Than Wind.
summary: In 2016, solar became cheaper than wind, marking a genuine turning point for world energy. Clean power is no longer the expensive idealist's option; it is simply the best deal.

title: A Joystick-Controlled Robot That Peels a Membrane 1/100th of a mm Thick.
summary: Surgeons used a joystick-controlled robot to peel a membrane a hundredth of a millimeter thick. Precision beyond the steadiest human hand, opening the door to eye operations once thought impossible.

title: The Stem-Cell Bio-Ink for 3D Printing Living Tissue.
summary: Scientists developed a bio-ink made with stem cells that can 3D-print living tissue. Printing with life itself is no longer science fiction; it is a laboratory reality inching toward medicine.

title: Rwanda Began Commercial Drone Deliveries of Blood.
summary: Rwanda launched commercial drone deliveries of blood, turning toys for some into life-savers for others. The country skipped straight to the future of logistics, one lifesaving drop at a time.

title: Tega: The Squishy Robot Teaching Preschoolers Spanish.
summary: Tega, a squishy little social robot, helps preschoolers learn Spanish by reading faces and playing along. Proof that the best teachers sometimes come with fur, patience, and endless enthusiasm.

title: Singapore's Self-Driving Cars Can Be Hailed With a Smartphone.
summary: In Singapore, self-driving cars could be summoned with a smartphone tap, making autonomy feel ordinary. The future of transport arrived not with a bang, but with a ride request.

title: Satellites Can Pinpoint Poverty Where Surveys Can't.
summary: Researchers found that satellite images can pinpoint poverty in places surveys never reach. From orbit, we can finally see the people the data forgot, and aim help where it matters most.

title: The World's First Robot-Assisted Operation Inside the Human Eye.
summary: At Oxford's John Radcliffe Hospital, the Preceyes robot performed the world's first robot-assisted operation inside the human eye. Tremor-free precision in a space smaller than a coin: a landmark for surgery.

title: You'll Love Your Robot More If You Assemble It Yourself.
summary: Research found the IKEA effect works on robots: people who assemble their own robot like it more and feel real ownership. Build it yourself, love it more: a hopeful hint about how humans and machines will bond.

title: Digital-Age Donations: USB Sticks for North Korea.
summary: Campaigners sought USB sticks to carry outside information into North Korea, digital-age donations for a closed country. Sometimes the mightiest technology is a thumb drive full of the world.

title: This Man Controls a Robotic Arm With His Thoughts.
summary: A prosthetic arm anchored directly to the skeleton and controlled by thought alone. Independence, restored by engineering.

title: Translation Apps Are Quietly Making the World Closer.
summary: Translation apps are quietly dissolving language barriers, making the world a little closer every day. The internet made the world smaller; translation makes it closer.

title: Satellites Are Measuring Economies in Real Time.
summary: Satellites with cheap cameras and big data are now measuring economies in near real time. A whole new way to see how the world is doing.

title: The $70,000 Exoskeleton That Helps the Paralyzed Walk.
summary: A $70,000 exoskeleton is helping paralyzed people walk, and it is already approved in the US and the EU. Bionic legs, now real and available.

title: Hi-Tech Agriculture Is Freeing the Farmer From His Fields.
summary: Satellite steering, drones, and sensor fields are doing the fieldwork so farmers don't have to. High-tech agriculture is freeing growers from the grind, one precise pass at a time.

title: Why Gene Editing Has Scientists So Excited.
summary: Scientists see a future where they go straight to the root cause of disease and repair the broken gene. That is the promise of gene editing, and the excitement is earned.

title: The Terminator-2 3D Printer: Solid Objects From Liquid in Minutes.
summary: The Terminator-2-inspired CLIP printer grows solid objects from liquid in minutes, 25 to 100 times faster than before. 3D printing just got a serious upgrade.

title: Weavers Turn Silk Into Diabetes Test Strips at a Third of the Cost.
summary: Weavers turned silk into diabetes test strips at a third of the usual cost. Traditional craft met modern medicine, and patients save.

title: The Hand of a Superhero: 3D-Printed Prosthetics Kids Actually Want.
summary: Superhero-styled, 3D-printed prosthetics give kids hands they actually want to wear, at a fraction of the cost. Prosthetics that celebrate rather than hide.

title: A Paralyzed Man Walked Again on Brain Power Alone.
summary: A paralyzed man walked again on brain power alone, with a UCI system that bypassed his spinal cord. His brain reached his legs without the wires in between.

title: How Robots, Drones, and New Disaster Tech Are Saving Lives.
summary: From robots to drones, a new generation of disaster technology is reaching survivors faster than ever. When every minute counts, machines are learning to do some of the bravest work of all.

title: Robots and Healthcare: Early Days, Promising Signs.
summary: A 2015 look at robots in healthcare found early days with genuinely promising signs. Even the first machines hinted at what was coming: robots as helpers in the hospital, not replacements for the humans.

title: The Cyborg Cockroach That Could Search Collapsed Buildings.
summary: Texas A&M researchers wired a tiny microcontroller into a cockroach's nervous system, creating a controllable insect that can squeeze into collapsed buildings. Nature's best explorer, upgraded with a remote control for search and rescue.

title: A 20-Year-Old Invented a Life-Saving Smart Wheelchair.
summary: A 20-year-old inventor built a smart wheelchair that could save lives. Youth, ingenuity, and a chair that changes everything.

title: Transplant Surgery Got a Paralyzed Man Walking Again.
summary: Transplant surgery got a paralyzed man walking again. In the doctor's words: this is just fantastic.

title: Controlling Google Glass With Brainwaves.
summary: Brainwaves are becoming a remote control for Google Glass. For people with limited abilities, this hands-free tech could do wonders.

title: The Nobel for the Brain's Inner GPS.
summary: The Nobel honored the discovery of the brain's inner GPS, the place and grid cells that map our world. A beautiful reward for decoding how we find our way.

title: "Scientists Make Telepathy Breakthrough."
summary: Scientists demonstrated brain-to-brain communication, sending messages directly between minds. Telepathy moved from science fiction to the lab bench.

title: A Robot Will Beam Live Moon Pictures to Your Headset.
summary: A robot is beaming live pictures from the Moon straight to your headset. The lunar surface, streamed like a live event.

title: A Robot That Helps Autistic Pupils Build Social Skills.
summary: A robot is helping autistic pupils build social skills, working alongside human support as a patient practice partner. Tech that meets kids where they are.

title: The Diabetes Patients Hacking Together Their Own Bionic Pancreas.
summary: Frustrated by waiting, diabetes patients built their own DIY artificial pancreas systems, tuning them to their bodies. Patient ingenuity at its best: people refusing to sit still while the perfect product was still in a lab.

title: Peek: The Smartphone Eye-Exam Kit That Could End Avoidable Blindness.
summary: Peek turns a smartphone into a full eye-exam kit, bringing diagnosis to villages that have never seen an eye doctor. Since most blindness is avoidable, this little adapter could end more of it than almost anything else.

title: A Five-Year-Old Got a 3D-Printed Prosthetic Hand for £50.
summary: A five-year-old received a 3D-printed prosthetic hand costing just 50 pounds, a fraction of traditional prices. Childhood, with two hands to play with: printed, affordable, and life-changing.

title: A Swarm of 1,024 Robots Working With No Central Intelligence.
summary: Harvard's 1,024 kilobots cooperated as a swarm with no central intelligence, each tiny robot following simple rules. A thousand simple robots, one smart crowd: the power of small minds working together.

title: The Smartshoe That Gives Directions Through Vibrations.
summary: An Indian startup built a smartshoe that guides wearers through vibrations, designed with the visually impaired in mind. Directions you feel instead of see: independence, one buzz at a time.

title: Training Robots to Paint, Build, and Play.
summary: Researchers are training robots to paint, build, and play, teaching machines the joyful skills, not just the useful ones. A robot that can play is a robot that hints at something more.

title: The Rowbot: A Roomba for the Cornfield.
summary: The Rowbot is a Roomba for the cornfield, fertilizing plant by plant to cut runoff. Small robot, cleaner rivers, smarter farming.

title: Batteryless Devices That Talk Over Wi-Fi Using Ambient Backscatter.
summary: University of Washington engineers built devices that communicate over Wi-Fi with no battery at all, harvesting ambient signals. Electronics that never need charging: the humblest, greenest trick in wireless.
